questions.stem: Highlight the findings from the head-to-toe assessment that need follow-up.

segments.text: drowsy and oriented to person and place only, a change from a week ago
a weaker left grip with drift of the left arm
a stage 2 pressure injury on the sacrum
has been incontinent of urine since yesterday

rationale.correct: A systematic head-to-toe assessment finds the subtle neurologic signs and the skin and elimination problems.

perOption.s2: A new change in level of consciousness.
perOption.s6: Pronator drift shows subtle motor weakness.
perOption.s8: Normal; a baseline to compare against.
perOption.s12: A skin finding that needs a care plan.
perOption.s14: New incontinence can reflect the neurologic change.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues on a head-to-toe assessment.

questions.stem: For each finding, choose the most likely explanation.

cells.text: Confusion and drowsiness developing over a week, 3 weeks after a head injury

options.text: A slowly expanding chronic subdural hematoma
A lesion on the right side of the brain
Raises the risk of a slowly growing bleed after minor trauma
Protects against stroke and makes a bleed unlikely

rationale.correct: Subacute confusion with focal signs weeks after a head injury on an anticoagulant suggests a chronic subdural.

perOption.b1:a: Older adults on anticoagulants bleed slowly from torn bridging veins.
perOption.b1:b: The change is new and recent.
perOption.b1:d: Possible contributor, but focal signs point to the brain.
perOption.b2:a: Motor pathways cross, matching the right-sided head injury.
perOption.b3:b: It prevents clots but raises bleeding risk.

questions.stem: Place the first actions in the correct order.

items.text: Assist with the lumbar puncture once the provider confirms it is safe

rationale.correct: Precautions, cultures, dexamethasone with the first antibiotic, then the lumbar puncture if safe.

perOption.b: Taken before antibiotics but without delaying them.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Carbidopa-levodopa at home times. Haloperidol added to allergies/intolerances. Swallow assessment. Cooling. IV fluids. Monitor CK.

questions.stem: The client is ready to get up for the first time with the physical therapist. Place the nurse's actions in order.

items.text: Use a gait belt and walker
Check lying and standing blood pressure
Cue large steps and a rhythm if the client freezes
Sit the client on the bed edge with feet flat before standing
Time the walk about 1 hour after a levodopa dose

rationale.correct: Time mobility with the medicine, check for orthostasis, stand in stages, and use aids and cues.

perOption.a: Mobility is best at peak effect.
perOption.b: Parkinson drugs and the disease cause orthostatic hypotension.

caseStudies.title: Head-to-toe assessment that uncovers a chronic subdural hematoma

exhibits.title: Medical unit, admission 1500
exhibits.body:
An 81-year-old client is admitted from home for "weakness and not eating." The client takes apixaban for atrial fibrillation and fell in the garden 3 weeks ago, hitting the head; the family says the client "seemed fine." Head-to-toe assessment by the admitting nurse:
General: drowsy but rousable, slow to answer, oriented to person and place only (family says sharp until a week ago).
Head and eyes: healed scalp bruise on the right; pupils 3 mm, equal and reactive; mild left facial droop when smiling.
Neck: supple.
Chest and lungs: clear; respirations 16/min.
Heart: irregularly irregular, 82/min; BP 152/88 mm Hg.
Abdomen: soft, bowel sounds present; last bowel movement 4 days ago.
Arms and legs: left hand grip weaker than right; left arm drifts down when held out with eyes closed.
Skin: stage 2 pressure injury on the sacrum, 2 x 3 cm; heels intact.
Elimination: incontinent of urine since yesterday.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 0200
exhibits.body: A 19-year-old college student who lives in a dormitory has had a severe headache, fever and vomiting since last evening. The client keeps the eyes closed in the light, and bending the neck forward causes pain. A purple, non-blanching rash is appearing on the legs.

exhibits.title: Surgical unit, postoperative day 1
exhibits.body: A 72-year-old client with Parkinson disease had a hip fracture repair yesterday. At home the client takes carbidopa-levodopa at 0700, 1100, 1500 and 1900, and rasagiline. Since surgery, doses were given at 0900 and 2100 only. Today the client is rigid, cannot turn in bed, has a soft voice and coughs when drinking. The client was given haloperidol 2 mg overnight for confusion.

exhibits.title: Neurology clinic
exhibits.body: A 32-year-old client with relapsing multiple sclerosis has had blurred, painful vision in the right eye for 3 days and new numbness and weakness of the right leg. The client also needs to urinate urgently and leaks before reaching the toilet. Symptoms got worse after a hot shower. The client takes fingolimod.

rows.label: Right eye
cells: Reduced acuity, pain on eye movement, red colors look washed out

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
